title: Present tenses: forms and uses
intro: Read this before the questions on the present tenses. Every tense has a FORM (how to build it) and a USE (when to choose it).

blocks.title: present simple
items: **Form:** subject + base verb. Add **-s** for he, she, it: She **works**. I **work**.
**Negative:** do / does + not + base verb: She **does not work**. They **do not work**.
**Question:** Do / Does + subject + base verb: **Does** she **work**?
**Use:** facts, habits and timetables: Water boils at 100 degrees. He plays football on Sundays.

blocks.title: present continuous
items: **Form:** am / is / are + verb-**ing**: She **is working**. I **am working**.
**Negative:** am / is / are + not + verb-ing: They **are not working**.
**Question:** Am / Is / Are + subject + verb-ing: **Are** they **working**?
**Use:** things happening now, temporary actions, and fixed plans: Look! It **is raining**.

blocks.title: spelling rules
items: he / she / it: add **-s** (works). After s, sh, ch, x, o add **-es**: watches, goes, fixes. Consonant + y becomes **-ies**: studies (but plays).
-ing: drop a silent **e** (make, making). After one short vowel, double the last consonant: run, **running**; sit, **sitting**.
After **does**, the verb is always the base form: She does not work (not *works*).

blocks.title: verbs that avoid the continuous
blocks.body: Verbs of state, such as **know, like, love, want, need, believe, own, understand**, are normally not used in the continuous. Say I **know** the answer, not I am knowing.
Time words: **always, usually, every day, never** point to the present simple. **Now, at the moment, today, these days, look!** point to the present continuous.
